status_sentence.QUEUED: Accepted and written down. A worker has not picked it up yet.
status_sentence.ASSIGNED: A node has been chosen and the work has been handed to it.
status_sentence.BUILDING: The node is cloning, installing and compiling.
status_sentence.PUBLISHING: The release is going in front of visitors. This cannot be cancelled.
status_sentence.CANCELLED: Somebody stopped it before it finished.
status_sentence.SUPERSEDED: A newer deployment overtook it while it was still waiting, so it never ran.

list.title: Deployments
list.description_site: Every build of this site, newest first. Publishing is a symlink swap, so going live and going back are both instant.
list.description_app: Every deployment of this app, newest first. Each one replaces the container with a fresh one from the image it names.
list.today_hint: Counted per organization across every service, and it is a rolling twenty-four hours rather than a calendar day. A rollback counts too: it is a deployment, it just does not build anything.
list.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so deploying, cancelling and rolling back are off. The history and every build log are still open to you.

detail.title: Deployment #{sequence}
detail.status_banner_current: This release is what visitors are being served.
detail.status_banner_succeeded: Published, and something newer has taken over since.
detail.status_banner_running: Still moving. This page follows the build as it goes.
detail.status_banner_terminal: Nothing further will happen to this deployment.

facts.title: Details
facts.author: Author
facts.no_node_yet: No node has taken it yet
facts.app_no_release_dir: An app has no release directory - it runs an image
facts.nothing_published: Nothing has been published for this deployment

history.label: deployments
history.empty_description: Every deployment of this service will be listed here with its build log, and any successful one can be rolled back to in a tap. Start one above.

timeline.title: Progress
timeline.queued_detail: Accepted and written down, waiting for a worker to pick it up.
timeline.assigned_detail_waiting: Waiting for a node with room for it.
timeline.assigned_detail_done: A node was chosen and the work was sent to it.
timeline.building_detail: Cloning, installing and compiling on the node, in a throwaway container.
timeline.publishing_detail_app: Starting a container from the new image and retiring the old one.
timeline.publishing_detail_rollback: Pointing the live symlink back at the release that is already on disk.
timeline.publishing_detail_site: Swapping the live symlink onto the new release directory. No downtime, and not cancellable.
timeline.detail_live: This is what visitors are being served.
timeline.detail_superseded_past: It was published and something newer has taken over since. It can be rolled back to.

viewer.dropped_notice: This build printed more than this page can hold. The first {dropped} lines were dropped; everything since is below.
viewer.empty_ended: This deployment produced no build output. An app is deployed by handing its node a spec, so there is nothing to compile and nothing to print.
viewer.empty_running: Waiting for the node to start printing…

retention.app_body: An app is deployed as an image, so nothing on the node is swept and every successful deployment in this list stays available to roll back to. Rolling back restarts the exact digest that was running, not whatever the tag points at today.
retention.app_restorable_none: There is no earlier successful deployment to go back to yet.
retention.app_restorable_count: {count} {count, plural, one {release} other {releases}} to roll back to.
retention.site_body: The node keeps the last {count} release{suffix} of this site on disk. Anything older is deleted from the node and drops out of this list, because a rollback to a directory that is gone would fail.
retention.footnote: The live release is never swept, and neither is the one a live rollback points back at - so a site serving release #3 after six later deploys keeps #3 whatever the limit says.

start.reason_read_only: You have read access to this organization, so you cannot start a deployment.
start.reason_spent: This organization has used all {limit} of today's deployments. The count resets on the hour, twenty-four hours after each one was started.
start.app_card_desc: An app is deployed by handing its node a spec naming the image it should run.
start.app_hint_default: The container is replaced with one started from the image in this service’s settings. Change the image there first if that is what you meant to update.
start.site_card_desc: The build runs on the node holding this site and only swaps the live release when it succeeds.
start.no_repo_hint: This site has no repository set, so deploying from Git is not offered. Add one under Settings and every push to its branch can build automatically.

git_form.ref_hint: Leave this empty to build {branch}, the branch this service is set to.
git_form.explanation: wisper clones {url}, builds it on the node holding this service and swaps the release directory over when the build succeeds. Nothing goes down while it runs.

archive_form.choose_zip: Choose a zip of the site
archive_form.drag_hint: Or drag one here. The zip is unpacked into a new release directory.

webhook.title: Deploy on push
webhook.desc_on: Every push to {branch} starts a deployment.
webhook.desc_off: Automatic deployment is off, so a push is recorded and nothing is built.
webhook.instructions_github: Add this as a webhook with content type application/json and the push event only.
webhook.instructions_gitlab: Add this under Settings → Webhooks with the push events trigger.
webhook.security_note_github: GitHub signs each delivery with this service’s webhook secret and wisper checks it before reading a byte of the body.
webhook.security_note_gitlab: GitLab sends this service’s webhook secret as a token header and wisper checks it before reading a byte of the body.
webhook.security_note_common: The secret was generated when the service was created and the panel does not display it again. A delivery signed with anything else is answered 401, and the reason appears in the provider’s own delivery log.

cancel.confirm_body: The build stops where it is. Whatever is live now stays live, and nothing that has already been published is undone.

rollback.confirm_body: Visitors get {what} again, usually within seconds - the release is still on the node, so nothing is rebuilt. This is recorded as a new deployment, and whatever is live now stays in the history and can be rolled back to in turn.
